text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGER: High error rate to authz proxy -> 429s from external IdP (vendor reported). Affected: user login flows + console access. Paging sre-oncall.

sre-oncall: I see spike in 5xx/429 on the authz-proxy upstream. First noticed ~12:03 UTC. Dashboard: /authz/proxy/* latency jumps. Users hitting web login and API token exchange failing.

mike: Confirmed. Token exchange endpoint returns 429 from vendor (rate-limited). We proxy those responses back as 502/429 depending on path. Logs: `authz_proxy.go: tokenExchange upstream 429 body: {\"error\":\"rate_limited\"}`.

laura: Are we seeing internal retries causing amplification? Traffic pattern shows burst from our lambda token refresh jobs too.

sre-oncall: Yes we have a retry storm for background refresh. Putting token-refresh jobs into backoff now.

amy: Support queue spiking, customers reporting "can't sign in" and some reports of console 500s. Two customers on Dedicated reported admin console access blocked.

jon: Need immediate customer comms. Can we say "we're investigating third-party auth provider rate limiting"?

raj: Security note: no evidence of malicious activity, looks like vendor throttling due to their internal rollout. Will keep monitoring.

sre-oncall: Mitigations in progress:
- throttling client-side token refreshes (feature flag rollback)
- enable cached session acceptance for console where safe
- failover route to vendor-backup endpoint (tiered)

mike: I'm running a quick failover test to the vendor's secondary endpoint:
```bash
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://idp-secondary.example.com/oauth/token
```
Response is currently 200 for a small % of requests. Secondary is flaky but better than direct 429s.

laura: I've pushed a temporary routing rule to send interactive logins to secondary endpoint (canary 10%). If that proves stable, increase to 50%.

sre-oncall: Also adding a header to mark requests that'll skip aggressive retries: `X-RW-Skip-Retry: 1` so our gateway doesn't amplify.

amy: Drafting a short status message for status.redwood.ai and support customers: "We are experiencing login failures due to rate limiting at our identity provider. We are mitigating by routing interactive logins to a secondary endpoint and throttling background refresh jobs. More updates in 30m." OK to post?

jon: Yes go ahead. Add approximate affected percentage if we can.

amy: Current estimate ~3-7% of logins failing across regions, consoles affected for a subset of admin users. Posting now.

incident-bot: Status page updated: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/RED-2024-2042 (posted by amy).

mike: Quick note on token verification errors: some downstream services reject tokens that hit the secondary endpoint due to slightly different token metadata (audience claim). I'm preparing a compatibility shim to accept both aud values for the short window.

laura: Can we avoid a wide rollback? Last time we saw a big spike when background workers all retried simultaneously. I've disabled non-critical background refresh across regions.

raj: For compliance: log retention for these auth failures is enabled. If customers request, we can provide request-level logs excluding PII.

sre-2: Oncall handoff in 40 minutes. If we don't have stabilization by then, I'll take next 2h to follow-through.

sre-oncall: Current status: routing canary -> 10% to secondary, background refresh throttled, retry suppression header in place. Error rate dropped from 28% to ~9% after canary. Still seeing intermittent 429s returned to a portion of API clients.

amy: Support update posted to affected customers; proactive outreach to top 5 affected accounts underway. Two customers escalated to SEs.

jon: Action items:
- mike: finish compatibility shim and deploy as hotfix (15m)
- laura: increase canary if stable to 50% (monitor 5m)
- sre-oncall: keep retry suppression and monitor error rate; escalate to vendor if >15% persists
- amy: continue customer comms & update status page every 30m

mike: Hotfix pushed to staging, smoke tests green. Deploying to prod in 5.

laura: Increasing canary to 50% now. Watchting dashboards.

sre-oncall: Error rate down to 4% after ramp. CPU on authz-proxy normalized.

incident-bot: :white_check_mark: Resolution criteria met: error rate <5% sustained for 10m. Marking incident as "mitigated".

amy: Updating status page to "mitigated" and sending recap to affected customers.

jon: Postmortem owners?: mike (auth path) + laura (routing & ops) + raj (security) + amy (customer impact). Please schedule follow-up and root-cause analysis.

sre-2: Handoff accepted. Will follow up re: vendor postmortem request and cleanup of temporary routing rules in 1h.

sre-oncall: Leaving notes in the incident doc and slack thread. Thanks team. :thumbsup:

mike: Quick follow-up: vendor confirmed they rolled out a throttling change that regressed for burst traffic. They say a rollback is in progress. Will coordinate for a joint postmortem.

laura: Reminder: remove `X-RW-Skip-Retry` header and revert routing after vendor confirms stability.

amy: Final status update posted to status page and support cases closed where resolved.

incident-bot: Incident transitioned to post-incident review queue. Tags: auth, third-party, vendor-rate-limit, handoff."
